pred_diagnosis: Giant Cell Tumor of the Tendon Sheath

2: While ganglion cysts are common in the wrist and can cause nerve compression, the atypical biphasic contrast enhancement pattern on MRI makes this diagnosis less likely than a soft tissue tumor, although the presence of a target sign and the cystic nature of the mass still make it a consideration.
4: The tumor's location on the radial side of the wrist, the presence of a target sign on MRI, and the biphasic contrast enhancement pattern are consistent with a giant cell tumor of the tendon sheath, which is a type of soft tissue tumor known to occur in the wrist and hand and can cause nerve compression symptoms.
